basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 21.' and it opens '(Vers. 21.) Et dedit illis cibaria in via. Verbum SEDA (צדה), quod hic omnes ore consono,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 21.) Et dedit illis cibaria in via. Verbum SEDA (צדה), quod hic omnes ore consono, ἐπισιτισμὸν, id est, cibaria, vel sitarcia interpretati sunt, in Psalterio quoque habetur. Ubi enim nostri legunt, Viduam ejus benedicens benedicam (Psal. CXXXI, 15), (licet in plerisque codicibus pro vidua, hoc est pro χήρᾳ, nonnulli legant θήραν), in Hebraeo habet SEDA (צידה), id est, Cibaria ejus benedicens benedicam. Porro θήραν venationem magis potest sonare, quam fruges; tametsi moris sit Aegyptiorum θήραν etiam far vocare, quod nunc corrupte atheran nuncupant.
